sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__禮樂志第十						唐書二十翰林學士兼龍圖閣學士朝散大夫給事中知制誥充史館脩撰臣歐陽脩奉敕撰五曰凶禮。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Treatise on Rites and Music 10						Book of Tang 20: Hanlin Academician and Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, Grand Master for Palace Audience, Attendant Gentleman with Authority to Draft Imperial Rescripts, Compiler at the Historical Archive by Imperial Commission, Ouyang Xiu, Fifth: Inauspicious Rites.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Treatise on Rites and Music 10						Book of Tang, Volume 20 — compiled by imperial order of Ouyang Xiu, Hanlin Academician and Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, Grand Master for Palace Audience, Attendant Gentleman with Authority to Draft Imperial Rescripts, and Compiler at the Historical Archive. Fifth: Inauspicious Rites.

sentences.zh: 周禮五禮，二曰凶禮。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, among the Five Rites, the second is Inauspicious Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou list five ritual categories; the second is inauspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 唐初，徙其次第五，而李義府、許敬宗以為凶事非臣子所宜言，遂去其國卹一篇，由是天子凶禮闕焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, its order was moved to fifth; Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong held that inauspicious matters were not what subjects should speak of, so they removed the section on national mourning, and thereby the Son of Heaven's inauspicious rites were left void.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang moved it to fifth place. Li Yifu and Xu Jingzong argued that subjects should not discuss inauspicious matters, removed the chapter on national mourning, and left the emperor's mourning rites undocumented.

sentences.zh: 至國有大故，則皆臨時采掇附比以從事，事已，則諱而不傳，故後世無考焉。

translations.literal: When the state had a great calamity, all gathered and compared precedents ad hoc to proceed; once the affair was done, it was tabooed and not transmitted, so later ages have no means to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophe struck, officials improvised from scattered precedents; once the crisis passed, the records were suppressed, so later ages cannot reconstruct them.

sentences.zh: 至開元制禮，惟著天子賑卹水旱、遣使問疾、弔死、舉哀、除服、臨喪、冊贈之類，若五服與諸臣之喪葬、衰麻、哭泣，則頗詳焉。

translations.literal: By the Kaiyuan ritual code, only the Son of Heaven's relief for flood and drought, dispatching envoys to inquire after illness, condolence for the dead, raising lamentation, removing mourning dress, attending funerals, and bestowing posthumous titles by edict were set down; as for the five grades of mourning dress and officials' funerals, hemp garments, and weeping, these were rather detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan code recorded imperial relief for disasters, illness envoys, condolence visits, court mourning, removing mourning dress, attending funerals, and posthumous enfeoffment. The five mourning grades and officials' burial, hemp dress, and weeping were treated in detail.

sentences.zh: 凡四方之水、旱、蝗，天子遣使者持節至其州，位于庭，使者南面，持節在其東南，長官北面，寮佐、正長、老人在其後，再拜，以授制書。

translations.literal: Whenever there was flood, drought, or locusts in the four directions, the Son of Heaven dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to that province; he took position in the courtyard, the envoy faced south with credentials southeast of him, the chief official faced north, aides, headmen, and elders behind him; they bowed twice and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: For regional flood, drought, or locust plague, the emperor sent a credentialed envoy to the province. In the courtyard the envoy faced south, credentials to his southeast; the prefect faced north with staff and elders behind; all bowed twice and received the edict.

sentences.zh: 其問疾亦如之，其主人迎使者於門外，使者東面，主人西面，再拜而入。

translations.literal: Inquiring after illness was the same; the host received the envoy outside the gate, the envoy faced east and the host west, bowed twice and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Illness inquiries followed the same form: the host met the envoy outside the gate; envoy east, host west; they bowed twice and entered.

sentences.zh: 其問婦人之疾，則受勞問者北面。

translations.literal: When inquiring after a woman's illness, the one receiving the visit faced north.
translations.idiomatic: For a woman's illness, the person receiving the envoy faced north.

sentences.zh: 若舉哀之日，為位於別殿，文武三品以上入哭于庭，四品以下哭于門外。

translations.literal: On a day of raising lamentation, positions were set in a separate hall; civil and military officials of third rank and above entered to weep in the courtyard, fourth rank and below wept outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: On a court mourning day, seats were arranged in a side hall. Officials of third rank and above wept in the courtyard; fourth rank and below, outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 有司版奏「中嚴」、「外辦」。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported by plaque: "Inner vigilance" and "Outer readiness."
translations.idiomatic: Officers announced by plaque: "Inner vigilance" and "Outer readiness."

sentences.zh: 皇帝已變服而哭，然後百官內外在位者皆哭，十五舉音，哭止而奉慰。

translations.literal: After the emperor had changed dress and wept, then all officials within and without in position wept, fifteen utterances of sound; when weeping ceased they offered consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed into mourning dress and wept first; then all present officials wept fifteen cries, stopped, and offered consolation.

sentences.zh: 其除服如之。

translations.literal: Removing mourning dress was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Removing mourning dress followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服：一品錫衰，三品以上緦衰，四品以下疑衰。

translations.literal: The emperor's dress: first rank, tin mourning; third rank and above, finest hemp mourning; fourth rank and below, doubtful hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore tin mourning for first rank, finest hemp for third rank and above, and doubtful hemp for fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 服期者，三朝晡止；

translations.literal: For those of fixed mourning term, morning and dusk sessions only;
translations.idiomatic: For fixed-term mourning, sessions at morning and dusk only;

sentences.zh: 大功，朝晡止；

translations.literal: greater hemp, morning and dusk only;
translations.idiomatic: greater hemp mourning, morning and dusk only;

sentences.zh: 小功以下，一哀止。

translations.literal: lesser hemp and below, one lamentation and stop.
translations.idiomatic: lesser hemp and below, a single cry and stop.

sentences.zh: 晡，百官不集。

translations.literal: At dusk, officials did not assemble.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, officials did not gather.

sentences.zh: 若為蕃國君長之喪，則設次于城外，向其國而哭，五舉音止。

translations.literal: If for the mourning of a foreign ruler, then a tent was set outside the city and they wept toward his state, five utterances of sound and stop.
translations.idiomatic: For a foreign ruler's death, a tent was pitched outside the walls and the court wept toward his realm, five cries and stop.

sentences.zh: 若臨喪，則設大次於其門西，設素裀榻於堂上。

translations.literal: If attending a funeral, then a great tent was set west of the gate, and a plain rush couch on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: For attending a funeral, a great tent west of the gate and a plain rush couch in the hall were prepared.

sentences.zh: 皇帝小駕、鹵簿，乘四望車，警蹕，鼓吹備而不作。

translations.literal: The emperor's light escort and guard of honor, riding the four-canopy carriage, with road cleared and music prepared but not played.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used the light escort and full guard, riding the four-canopy carriage; the route was cleared and musicians stood by but did not play.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至大次，易素服，從官皆易服，侍臣則不。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the great tent, he changed to plain dress; attendants all changed dress; personal attendants did not.
translations.idiomatic: At the great tent the emperor donned plain dress; attendants changed likewise, but personal attendants did not.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出次，喪主人免絰、釋杖、哭門外，望見乘輿，止哭而再拜，先入門右，西向。

translations.literal: The emperor left the tent; the mourning host removed the headband, set down the staff, and wept outside the gate; seeing the imperial carriage, he stopped weeping and bowed twice, entered first on the right, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the tent, the host removed headband and staff and wept at the gate; seeing the carriage, he ceased weeping, bowed twice, entered on the right, and faced west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至堂，升自阼階，即哭位。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the hall, he ascended by the eastern steps and took the place of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the hall by the eastern steps and took the mourning seat.

sentences.zh: 巫、祝各一人先升，巫執桃立于東南，祝執茢立于西南，戈者四人先後隨升。

translations.literal: One shaman and one invoker ascended first; the shaman held peach wood and stood southeast, the invoker held wormwood and stood southwest; four men with halberds followed up in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman and invoker went up first: the shaman with peach wood southeast, the invoker with wormwood southwest; four halberd bearers followed.

sentences.zh: 喪主人入廷再拜，敕引乃升，立戶內之東，西向。

translations.literal: The mourning host entered the court and bowed twice; only when led by edict did he ascend, standing east within the door, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host bowed twice in the court, then ascended only at imperial command, standing east inside the door, facing west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出，喪主人門外拜送。

translations.literal: When the emperor departed, the mourning host bowed in send-off outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor left, the host bowed in farewell outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝變服于次，乃還廬。

translations.literal: The emperor changed dress in the tent, then returned to the mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed dress in the tent, then returned to the mourning shed.

sentences.zh: 文、武常服。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials in regular dress.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials wore regular dress.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升車，鼓吹不作而入。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the carriage; music was not played on entering.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted; no music played on departure.

sentences.zh: 其以敕使冊贈，則受冊于朝堂，載以犢車，備鹵簿，至第。

translations.literal: When bestowing posthumous titles by edict envoy, the patent was received in the audience hall, loaded on a calf cart, with full guard of honor, to the residence.
translations.idiomatic: For edict-bestowed posthumous titles, the patent was received at court, carried on a calf cart with full guard to the deceased's home.

sentences.zh: 妃主以內侍為使，贈者以蠟印畫綬。

translations.literal: For consorts and princesses, inner attendants served as envoys; the gift bore wax seal and painted cord.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and princesses used inner attendants as envoys; gifts bore wax seals and painted cords.

sentences.zh: 冊贈必因其啟葬，既葬則受於靈寢，既除則受於廟。

translations.literal: Patent-bestowal must follow the opening of burial; if already buried, it was received at the spirit chamber; if mourning was ended, at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Patents were timed to the opening of burial; if burial was done, reception was at the spirit chamber; after mourning ended, at the temple.

sentences.zh: 主人公服而不哭，或單衣而介幘。

translations.literal: The host wore unhemmed dress and did not weep, or wore a single garment with a kerchief cap.
translations.idiomatic: The host wore plain mourning without weeping, or a single robe with kerchief cap.

sentences.zh: 受必有祭；

translations.literal: Reception required an offering;
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the patent required an offering;

sentences.zh: 未廟，受之寢。

translations.literal: if the temple was not yet established, reception was in the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: if no ancestral temple yet, reception was in the private chamber.

sentences.zh: 五服之制。

translations.literal: The system of the five mourning grades.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for the five mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 斬衰三年。

translations.literal: Severest hemp, three years.
translations.idiomatic: Severest hemp mourning: three years.

sentences.zh: 正服：子為父，女子子在室與已嫁而反室為父。

translations.literal: Regular dress: a son for his father; an unmarried daughter or a married daughter returned home for her father.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: son for father; unmarried daughter, or married daughter returned home, for father.

sentences.zh: 加服：嫡孫為後者為祖，父為長子。

translations.literal: Added dress: the eldest grandson as heir for his grandfather; a father for his eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Added mourning: heir-apparent grandson for grandfather; father for eldest son.

sentences.zh: 義服：為人後者為所後父，妻為夫，妾為君，國官為君。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: an adopted son for his adoptive father; a wife for her husband; a concubine for her lord; a state official for his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: adoptee for adoptive father; wife for husband; concubine for lord; state official for sovereign.

sentences.zh: 王公以下三月而葬，葬而虞，三虞而卒哭。

translations.literal: From kings and dukes downward, burial in three months; at burial, yu offering; three yu then end of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: From princes down, burial at three months; yu rites at burial; three yu, then end of weeping.

sentences.zh: 十三月小祥，二十五月大祥，二十七月禫祭。

translations.literal: At thirteen months, lesser felicity; at twenty-five months, greater felicity; at twenty-seven months, the unhemmed sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser felicity at thirteen months; greater at twenty-five; unhemmed sacrifice at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 齊衰三年。

translations.literal: Equal hemp, three years.
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp mourning: three years.

sentences.zh: 正服：子，父在為母。

translations.literal: Regular dress: a son, while his father lives, for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: son, while father lives, for mother.

sentences.zh: 加服：為祖後者，祖卒則為祖母，母為長子。

translations.literal: Added dress: for an heir of the grandfather, when the grandfather dies then for the grandmother; a mother for her eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Added mourning: heir for grandmother after grandfather's death; mother for eldest son.

sentences.zh: 義服：為繼母、慈母，繼母為長子，妾為君之長子。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a stepmother or nurturing mother; a stepmother for her eldest son; a concubine for her lord's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: stepmother or nurturing mother; stepmother for eldest son; concubine for lord's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 齊衰杖周。

translations.literal: Equal hemp with staff, one year.
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp with mourning staff: one year.

sentences.zh: 降服：父卒，母嫁及出妻之子為母，報，服亦如之。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: when the father has died, a son whose mother remarried or was divorced for his mother, return mourning, dress likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: after father's death, son of remarried or divorced mother for mother, with reciprocal mourning of the same grade.

sentences.zh: 正服：為祖後者，祖在為祖母。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for an heir of the grandfather, while the grandfather lives, for the grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: heir for grandmother while grandfather lives.

sentences.zh: 義服：父卒，繼母嫁，從，為之服報；

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: when the father has died and the stepmother remarries, if one follows her, dress return mourning for her;
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: after father's death, if stepmother remarries and one follows her, reciprocal mourning;

sentences.zh: 夫為妻。

translations.literal: a husband for his wife.
translations.idiomatic: husband for wife.

sentences.zh: 齊衰不杖周。

translations.literal: Equal hemp without staff, one year.
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp without staff: one year.

sentences.zh: 正服：為祖父母，為伯叔父，為兄弟，為眾子，為兄弟之子及女子子在室與適人者，為嫡孫，為姑、姊妹與無夫子，報，女子子與適人為祖父母，妾為其子。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for grandparents, for paternal uncles, for brothers, for younger sons, for brothers' sons and unmarried daughters or married daughters, for eldest grandson, for paternal aunts and sisters and childless wives, return mourning, daughters and married daughters for grandparents, a concubine for her son.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: grandparents, paternal uncles, brothers, younger sons, brothers' children (unmarried or married daughters), eldest grandson, aunts and sisters and childless wives (with reciprocal mourning), daughters for grandparents, concubine for son.

sentences.zh: 加服：女子子適人者為兄弟之為父後者。

translations.literal: Added dress: a married daughter for a brother who is heir of the father.
translations.idiomatic: Added mourning: married daughter for brother who is father's heir.

sentences.zh: 降服：妾為其父母，為人後者為其父母，報，女子子適人者為其父母。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: a concubine for her parents, an adopted son for his birth parents, return mourning, a married daughter for her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: concubine for parents; adoptee for birth parents (reciprocal); married daughter for parents.

sentences.zh: 義服：為伯叔母，為繼父同居者，妾為嫡妻，妾為君之庶子，婦為舅、姑，為夫之兄弟之子，舅、姑為嫡婦。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for paternal aunts by marriage, for a stepfather living together, a concubine for the principal wife, a concubine for her lord's younger sons, a daughter-in-law for parents-in-law, for a husband's brother's son, parents-in-law for the principal daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: paternal aunts-in-law; stepfather cohabiting; concubine for principal wife or lord's younger sons; daughter-in-law for in-laws; husband's brother's son; in-laws for principal daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 齊衰五月。

translations.literal: Equal hemp, five months.
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp mourning: five months.

sentences.zh: 正服：為曾祖父母，女子子在室及嫁者亦如之。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for great-grandparents; unmarried and married daughters likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: great-grandparents; unmarried and married daughters alike.

sentences.zh: 齊衰三月。

translations.literal: Equal hemp, three months.
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp mourning: three months.

sentences.zh: 正服：為高祖父母，女子子在室及嫁者亦如之。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for great-great-grandparents; unmarried and married daughters likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: great-great-grandparents; unmarried and married daughters alike.

sentences.zh: 義服：為繼父不同居者。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a stepfather not living together.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: stepfather not cohabiting.

sentences.zh: 其父卒母嫁，出妻之子為母，及為祖後，祖在為祖母，雖周除，仍心喪三年。

translations.literal: When the father has died and the mother remarries, a son of a divorced wife for his mother, and for an heir of the grandfather, while the grandfather lives for the grandmother—though the one-year term ends, heart mourning for three years still.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of remarried or divorced mothers, and heirs mourning grandmothers while grandfather lives, ended the one-year term outwardly but kept three years of heart mourning.

sentences.zh: 大功，長殤九月，中殤七月。

translations.literal: Greater hemp: long early death nine months, middle early death seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Greater hemp: long early death, nine months; middle early death, seven months.

sentences.zh: 正服：為子、女子子之長殤、中殤，為叔父之長殤、中殤，為姑、姊妹之長殤、中殤，為兄弟之長殤、中殤，為嫡孫之長殤、中殤，為兄弟之子、女子之長殤、中殤。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for a son's or daughter's long or middle early death; for a paternal uncle's long or middle early death; for an aunt's or sister's long or middle early death; for a brother's long or middle early death; for an eldest grandson's long or middle early death; for a brother's son's or daughter's long or middle early death.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: children's, paternal uncle's, aunt's or sister's, brother's, eldest grandson's, or brother's child's long or middle early death.

sentences.zh: 義服：為夫之兄弟之子、女子子之長殤、中殤。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a husband's brother's son's or daughter's long or middle early death.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: husband's brother's child's long or middle early death.

sentences.zh: 成人九月正服：為從兄弟，為庶孫。

translations.literal: For an adult, nine months regular dress: for second cousins, for younger grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Adults, nine months regular mourning: second cousins; younger grandsons.

sentences.zh: 降服：為女子子適人者，為姑、姊妹適人者報；

translations.literal: Reduced dress: for a married daughter, for an aunt or sister married, return mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: married daughter; married aunt or sister (reciprocal);

sentences.zh: 出母為女子子適人者，為兄弟之女適人者報；

translations.literal: a divorced mother for a married daughter, for a brother's daughter married, return mourning;
translations.idiomatic: divorced mother for married daughter; brother's married daughter (reciprocal);

sentences.zh: 為人後者為其兄弟與姑、姊妹在室者報。

translations.literal: an adopted son for his brothers and aunts and sisters at home, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: adoptee for brothers and unmarried aunts and sisters (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 義服：為夫之祖父母與伯叔父母報，為夫之兄弟女適人者報；

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a husband's grandparents and paternal uncles and aunts, return mourning; for a husband's brother's daughter married, return mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: husband's grandparents and paternal uncles and aunts (reciprocal); husband's brother's married daughter (reciprocal);

sentences.zh: 夫為人後者，其妻為本生舅、姑，為眾子之婦。

translations.literal: when the husband is an adopted son, his wife for her birth mother's brothers and sisters, for the younger sons' wives.
translations.idiomatic: if the husband is adopted, his wife mourns her birth mother's kin and the wives of younger sons.

sentences.zh: 小功五月殤。

translations.literal: Lesser hemp, five months for early death.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser hemp: five-month early death mourning.

sentences.zh: 正服：為子、女子子之下殤，為叔父之下殤，為姑、姊妹之下殤，為兄弟之下殤，為嫡孫之下殤，為兄弟之子、女子子之下殤，為從兄弟姊妹之長殤，為庶孫之長殤。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for a son's or daughter's lesser early death; for a paternal uncle's lesser early death; for an aunt's or sister's lesser early death; for a brother's lesser early death; for an eldest grandson's lesser early death; for a brother's son's or daughter's lesser early death; for a second cousin's long early death; for a younger grandson's long early death.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: children's, uncle's, aunt's or sister's, brother's, eldest grandson's, brother's child's, second cousin's long, or younger grandson's long lesser early death.

sentences.zh: 降服：為人後者為其兄弟之長殤，出嫁姑為姪之長殤，為人後者為其姑、姊妹之長殤。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: an adopted son for his brother's long early death; a married aunt for her nephew's long early death; an adopted son for his aunt's or sister's long early death.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: adoptee for brother's long early death; married aunt for nephew's long early death; adoptee for aunt's or sister's long early death.

sentences.zh: 義服：為夫之兄弟之子、女子子之下殤，為夫之叔父之長殤。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a husband's brother's son's or daughter's lesser early death; for a husband's paternal uncle's long early death.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: husband's brother's child's lesser early death; husband's paternal uncle's long early death.

sentences.zh: 成人正服：為從祖祖父報，為從祖父報，為從祖姑、姊妹在室者報，為從祖兄弟報，為從祖祖姑在室者報，為外祖父母，為舅及從母報。

translations.literal: For an adult, regular dress: for a father's second cousin, return mourning; for a father's cousin, return mourning; for a father's second cousin's unmarried aunt or sister, return mourning; for a father's second cousin's brother, return mourning; for a father's second cousin's paternal aunt at home, return mourning; for maternal grandparents; for a maternal uncle and maternal aunt, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Adult regular mourning: father's second cousin, father's cousin, their unmarried aunts or sisters, second-cousin brothers, father's second cousin's aunt at home (all reciprocal); maternal grandparents; maternal uncle and aunt (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 降服：為從父姊妹適人者報，為孫女適人者，為人後者為其姑、姊妹適人者報。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: for a father's sister married, return mourning; for a granddaughter married; an adopted son for his aunt or sister married, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: father's married sister (reciprocal); married granddaughter; adoptee for married aunt or sister (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 義服：為從祖祖母報，為從祖母報，為夫之姑、姊妹在室及適人者報，娣姒婦報，為同母異父兄弟姊妹報，為嫡母之父母兄弟從母，為庶母慈己者，為嫡孫之婦，母出為繼母之父母兄弟從母，嫂叔報。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: for a father's second cousin's wife, return mourning; for a father's cousin's wife, return mourning; for a husband's aunt or sister at home or married, return mourning; for sisters-in-law, return mourning; for half-siblings by the same mother, return mourning; for the principal mother's parents, brothers, and maternal aunts; for a concubine who nurtured one; for the principal grandson's wife; when the mother left home, for the stepmother's parents, brothers, and maternal aunts; elder brother's wife and younger brother's wife, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: father's second cousin's or cousin's wife (reciprocal); husband's aunts and sisters at home or married (reciprocal); sisters-in-law; maternal half-siblings (reciprocal); principal mother's kin; nurturing concubine; principal grandson's wife; stepmother's kin if mother left; sister-in-law and brother's wife (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 緦麻三月殤。

translations.literal: Finest hemp, three months for early death.
translations.idiomatic: Finest hemp: three-month early death mourning.

sentences.zh: 正服：為從父兄弟姊妹之中殤、下殤，為庶孫之中殤、下殤，為從祖叔父之長殤，為從祖兄弟之長殤，為舅及從母之長殤，為從父兄弟之子之長殤，為兄弟之孫長殤，為從祖姑、姊妹之長殤。

translations.literal: Regular dress: for a father's brother's middle or lesser early death; for a younger grandson's middle or lesser early death; for a father's cousin's long early death; for a father's second cousin's long early death; for a maternal uncle's or aunt's long early death; for a father's brother's son's long early death; for a brother's grandson's long early death; for a father's cousin's aunt's or sister's long early death.
translations.idiomatic: Regular mourning: paternal uncle's middle or lesser early death; younger grandson's middle or lesser; father's cousin's or second cousin's long early death; maternal uncle's or aunt's long; father's brother's son's long; brother's grandson's long; father's cousin's aunt's or sister's long.

sentences.zh: 降服：為人後者為其兄弟之中殤、下殤，為姪之中殤、下殤，出嫁姑為之報，為人後者為其姑、姊妹之中殤、下殤。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: an adopted son for his brother's middle or lesser early death; for a nephew's middle or lesser early death, a married aunt for this, return mourning; an adopted son for his aunt's or sister's middle or lesser early death.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: adoptee for brother's middle or lesser early death; nephew's middle or lesser (married aunt reciprocal); adoptee for aunt's or sister's middle or lesser.

sentences.zh: 義服：為人後者為從父兄弟之長殤，為夫之叔父之中殤、下殤，為夫之姑、姊妹之長殤。

translations.literal: Obligatory dress: an adopted son for a father's brother's long early death; for a husband's paternal uncle's middle or lesser early death; for a husband's aunt's or sister's long early death.
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning: adoptee for father's brother's long early death; husband's paternal uncle's middle or lesser; husband's aunt's or sister's long early death.

sentences.zh: 成人正服：為族兄弟，為族曾祖父報，為族祖父報，為族父報，為外孫，為曾孫、玄孫，為從母兄弟姊妹，為姑之子，為舅之子，為族曾祖姑在室者報，為族祖姑在室者報，為族姑在室者報。

translations.literal: For an adult, regular dress: for clan brothers; for a clan great-great-grandfather, return mourning; for a clan great-grandfather, return mourning; for a clan grandfather, return mourning; for a maternal grandson; for a great-grandson and great-great-grandson; for maternal cousins; for an aunt's son; for a maternal uncle's son; for a clan great-great-grandfather's unmarried aunt, return mourning; for a clan great-grandfather's unmarried aunt, return mourning; for a clan grandfather's unmarried aunt, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Adult regular mourning: clan brothers; clan great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather (reciprocal); maternal grandson; great-grandson and great-great-grandson; maternal cousins; aunt's son; maternal uncle's son; clan great-great-grandfather's, great-grandfather's, or grandfather's unmarried aunts (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 降服：為從祖姑、姊妹適人者報，女子子適人者為從祖父報，庶子為父後者為其母，為從祖姑適人者報，為人後者為外祖父母，為兄弟之孫女適人者報。

translations.literal: Reduced dress: for a father's cousin's aunt or sister married, return mourning; a married daughter for her father's cousin, return mourning; a younger son made heir for his mother; for a father's cousin's aunt married, return mourning; an adopted son for maternal grandparents; for a brother's granddaughter married, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced mourning: father's cousin's married aunt or sister (reciprocal); married daughter for father's cousin (reciprocal); younger son made heir for mother; father's cousin's married aunt (reciprocal); adoptee for maternal grandparents; brother's married granddaughter (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 義服；

translations.literal: Obligatory dress;
translations.idiomatic: Obligatory mourning;

sentences.zh: 為族曾祖母報，為族祖母報，為族母報，為庶孫之婦，女子子適人者為從祖伯叔母，為庶母，為乳母，為壻，為妻之父母，為夫之曾祖高祖父母，為夫之從祖祖父母報，為夫之從祖父母報，為夫之外祖父母報，為從祖兄弟之子，為夫之從父兄弟之妻，為夫之從父姊妹在室及適人者，為夫之舅及從母報。

translations.literal: for a clan great-great-grandmother, return mourning; for a clan great-grandmother, return mourning; for a clan grandmother, return mourning; for a younger grandson's wife; a married daughter for her father's paternal uncles' wives; for a birth mother; for a wet nurse; for a son-in-law; for a wife's parents; for a husband's great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather; for a husband's father's second cousin's grandparents, return mourning; for a husband's father's cousin's grandparents, return mourning; for a husband's maternal grandparents, return mourning; for a father's second cousin's son; for a husband's father's brother's wife; for a husband's father's sister at home or married; for a husband's maternal uncle and aunt, return mourning.
translations.idiomatic: clan great-great-grandmother, great-grandmother, grandmother (reciprocal); younger grandson's wife; married daughter for father's paternal uncles' wives; birth mother; wet nurse; son-in-law; wife's parents; husband's great-great-grandfather and great-grandfather; husband's father's second cousin's or cousin's grandparents (reciprocal); husband's maternal grandparents (reciprocal); father's second cousin's son; husband's father's brother's wife; husband's father's sister at home or married; husband's maternal uncle and aunt (reciprocal).

sentences.zh: 改葬：子為父母，妻妾為其夫，其冠服杖屨皆依儀禮。

translations.literal: Reburial: a son for his parents, a wife or concubine for her husband—the cap, dress, staff, and shoes all followed the Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Reburial: son for parents, wife or concubine for husband—cap, dress, staff, and shoes followed the Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 皇家所絕傍親無服者，皇弟、皇子為之皆降一等。

translations.literal: For collateral kin cut off by the imperial house, imperial younger brothers and imperial sons all reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Where the imperial house severed collateral ties, imperial younger brothers and sons reduced mourning one grade.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗以同爨緦而嫂叔乃無服，舅與從母親等而異服，詔侍中魏徵、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等議：「舅為母族，姨乃外戚它姓，舅固為重，而服止一時，姨喪乃五月，古人未達者也。

translations.literal: At first Taizong once noted that though they ate from one pot in finest hemp, yet elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband had no mourning dress, and maternal uncle and maternal aunt were equal kin yet different dress; he ordered Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others to discuss: "The maternal uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle is indeed weighty, yet dress lasts only a season, while aunt mourning is five months: the ancients did not penetrate this.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Taizong observed that kin eating from one pot wore finest hemp, yet brother's wife and younger brother's husband had no mourning; maternal uncle and aunt were equally close yet dressed differently. He ordered Wei Zheng, Linghu Defen, and others to debate: "The uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle weighs heavier, yet mourning lasts one season while the aunt's is five months: the ancients missed this."

sentences.zh: 於是服曾祖父母齊衰三月者，增以齊衰五月；

translations.literal: Thus for mourning great-grandparents in equal hemp three months, it was increased to equal hemp five months;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for great-grandparents in three-month equal hemp was raised to five months;

sentences.zh: 適子婦大功，增以期；

translations.literal: the principal son's wife in greater hemp was increased to fixed term;
translations.idiomatic: the principal son's wife, from greater hemp, was raised to fixed-term mourning;

sentences.zh: 眾子婦小功，增以大功；

translations.literal: the younger sons' wives in lesser hemp were increased to greater hemp;
translations.idiomatic: younger sons' wives, from lesser hemp, to greater hemp;

sentences.zh: 嫂叔服以小功五月報；

translations.literal: elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband, dress in lesser hemp five months, return mourning;
translations.idiomatic: brother's wife and younger brother's husband: lesser hemp five months, reciprocal;

sentences.zh: 其弟妻及夫兄亦以小功；

translations.literal: their younger brother's wife and husband's elder brother also in lesser hemp;
translations.idiomatic: younger brother's wife and husband's elder brother likewise in lesser hemp;

sentences.zh: 舅服緦，請與從母增以小功。

translations.literal: maternal uncle in finest hemp—request to increase with maternal aunt to lesser hemp.
translations.idiomatic: maternal uncle in finest hemp—petition to raise uncle and aunt together to lesser hemp.

sentences.zh: 」然律疏舅報甥，服猶緦。

translations.literal: " Yet in the law commentary the uncle, return mourning for nephew, dress was still finest hemp.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet the statutory commentary still had the uncle's reciprocal mourning for a nephew in finest hemp.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，長孫无忌以為甥為舅服同從母，則舅宜進同從母報。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era, Zhangsun Wuji held that since a nephew's dress for his uncle was the same as for a maternal aunt, the uncle's return mourning ought to advance to match the maternal aunt's.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianqing, Zhangsun Wuji argued that because a nephew mourned an uncle like a maternal aunt, the uncle's reciprocal mourning should match the aunt's grade.

sentences.zh: 又古庶母緦，今無服，且庶母之子，昆弟也，為之杖齊，是同氣而吉凶異，自是亦改服緦。

translations.literal: Also in antiquity birth mothers wore finest hemp; now there is no dress—and the birth mother's sons are brothers of one breath, yet for them equal hemp with staff, so same qi yet different fortune and misfortune; this too was changed to finest hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently birth mothers received finest hemp; now none—and their sons were full brothers, yet wore equal hemp with staff: same kin, different grief. This too was changed to finest hemp.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，武后請「父在，服母三年」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu requested: "While the father lives, mourn the mother three years."
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1, Empress Wu petitioned: "While the father lives, mourn the mother three years."

sentences.zh: 開元五年，右補闕盧履冰言：「禮，父在為母期，而服三年，非也，請如舊章。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing said: "In ritual, while the father lives one mourns the mother for a fixed term, yet dress for three years is wrong—please follow the old statute.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing said: "Rites prescribe a fixed term for mother while father lives; three-year dress is wrong—restore the old rule."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔幷議舅及嫂叔服，久而不能決。

translations.literal: " Then an edict ordered joint deliberation on dress for maternal uncles and elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband; long they could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered joint debate on mourning for maternal uncles and for brother's wife and younger brother's husband, but no decision came for a long time.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中書令蕭嵩等改脩五禮，於是父在為母齊衰三年。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Chief Minister Xiao Song and others revised the Five Rites, and thus while the father lived, mourning the mother in equal hemp three years.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, Chief Minister Xiao Song and others revised the Five Rites, restoring three-year equal hemp for the mother while the father lived.

sentences.zh: 諸臣之喪。

translations.literal: Mourning for officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites for officials.

sentences.zh: 有疾，齊於正寢，臥東首北墉下。

translations.literal: When ill, rest in the main chamber, lying east of head on the north wall base.
translations.idiomatic: In illness, the sick lay in the main chamber, head east on the north wall.

sentences.zh: 疾困，去衣，加新衣，徹樂，清掃內外。

translations.literal: When illness was grave, remove clothes, put on new clothes, stop music, sweep inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: When critically ill, clothing was changed, music stopped, and the house swept clean inside and out.

sentences.zh: 四人坐而持手足，遺言則書之屬纊。

translations.literal: Four men sat holding hands and feet; if there were last words, they were written on the attachment cord.
translations.idiomatic: Four attendants held hands and feet; final words were written on the attachment cord.

sentences.zh: 氣絕，寢於地。

translations.literal: When breath ceased, lay on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: At death, the body was laid on the ground.

sentences.zh: 男子白布衣，被髮徒跣；

translations.literal: Men wore white plain cloth, hair loose, barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: Men wore white plain cloth, with hair loose and bare feet;

sentences.zh: 婦人女子青縑衣，去首飾；

translations.literal: women and girls wore green silk, removed head ornaments;
translations.idiomatic: women and girls wore green silk and removed jewelry;

sentences.zh: 齊衰以下，丈夫素冠。

translations.literal: for equal hemp and below, men wore plain caps.
translations.idiomatic: those in equal hemp or lighter grades wore plain caps.

sentences.zh: 主人坐於牀東，啼踊無數。

translations.literal: The host sat east of the couch, wailing and leaping without number.
translations.idiomatic: The host sat east of the bed, wailing and leaping repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 眾主人在其後，兄弟之子以下又在其後，皆西面南上，哭。

translations.literal: Secondary hosts were behind him, younger sons of brothers and below behind them, all facing west ascending south, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Other hosts stood behind, then younger brothers' sons and below, all facing west, ranked south to north, weeping.

sentences.zh: 妻坐於牀西，妾及女子在其後，哭踊無數。

translations.literal: The wife sat west of the couch, concubines and women behind her, wailing and leaping without number.
translations.idiomatic: The wife sat west of the bed; concubines and women behind her wailed and leaped repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 兄弟之女以下又在其後，皆東面南上，籍藳坐哭。

translations.literal: Younger brothers' daughters and below behind them, all facing east ascending south, sitting on straw mats weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers' daughters and below faced east, ranked south to north, sitting on straw mats and weeping.

sentences.zh: 內外之際，隔以行帷。

translations.literal: Between inner and outer, separated by a traveling curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer mourners were divided by a traveling curtain.

sentences.zh: 祖父以下為帷東北壁下，南面西上；

translations.literal: Grandfather and below at the northeast wall under the curtain, facing south ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: Grandfathers and below sat northeast under the curtain, facing south, ranked west to east;

sentences.zh: 祖母以下為帷西北壁，南面東上。

translations.literal: grandmother and below at the northwest wall, facing south ascending east.
translations.idiomatic: grandmothers and below northwest, facing south, ranked east to west.

sentences.zh: 外姻丈夫於戶外東，北面西上；

translations.literal: Outer-affinal men east of the door outside, facing north ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: Male affines stood east of the outer door, facing north, ranked west to east;

sentences.zh: 婦人於主婦西北，南面東上。

translations.literal: women northwest of the principal wife, facing south ascending east.
translations.idiomatic: women northwest of the principal wife, facing south, ranked east to west.

sentences.zh: 諸內喪，則尊行丈夫及外親丈夫席位於前堂，若戶外之左右，俱南面。

translations.literal: For inner mourning, then senior men and outer-affinal men took seats in the front hall, as left and right of outside the door, all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: In inner mourning, senior men and male affines sat in the front hall or flanking the outer door, all facing south.

sentences.zh: 宗親戶東，西上；

translations.literal: Clan kin east of the door, ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: Clan kin east of the door, ranked west to east;

sentences.zh: 外親戶西，東上。

translations.literal: outer kin west of the door, ascending east.
translations.idiomatic: outer affines west of the door, ranked east to west.

sentences.zh: 凡喪，皆以服精粗為序，國官位於門內之東，重行北面西上，俱衺巾帕頭，舒薦坐；

translations.literal: For all mourning, order by fineness of dress; state officials at the east inside the gate, double ranks facing north ascending west, all with slanted kerchief headwrap, spread rush mats and sit;
translations.idiomatic: All mourners ranked by mourning grade. State officials sat inside the east gate, double file facing north west to east, slanted kerchiefs, on spread rush mats;

sentences.zh: 參佐位於門內之西，重行北面東上，素服，皆舒席坐，哭。

translations.literal: aides at the west inside the gate, double ranks facing north ascending east, plain dress, all on spread mats sitting, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: aides inside the west gate, double file facing north east to west in plain dress on rush mats, weeping.

sentences.zh: 斬衰，三日不食；

translations.literal: Severest hemp, three days without food;
translations.idiomatic: Severest hemp: no food for three days;

sentences.zh: 齊衰，二日不食；

translations.literal: equal hemp, two days without food;
translations.idiomatic: equal hemp: two days;

sentences.zh: 大功，三不食；

translations.literal: greater hemp, three meals omitted;
translations.idiomatic: greater hemp: skip three meals;

sentences.zh: 小功、緦麻，再不食。

translations.literal: lesser hemp and finest hemp, two meals omitted.
translations.idiomatic: lesser and finest hemp: skip two meals.

sentences.zh: 復於正寢。

translations.literal: Summoning back at the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning the soul back in the main chamber.

sentences.zh: 復者三人，以死者之上服左荷之，升自前東霤，當屋履危，北面西上。

translations.literal: Three summoners, bearing the deceased's upper garment on the left shoulder, ascended from the front east eaves, stood on the roof ridge facing north ascending west.
translations.idiomatic: Three summoners carried the deceased's upper garment over the left shoulder, climbed the front east eaves to the ridge, and faced north, west to east.

sentences.zh: 左執領，右執腰，招以左。

translations.literal: Left hand held the collar, right the waist, beckoning with the left.
translations.idiomatic: Left hand on the collar, right on the waist, beckoning with the left.

sentences.zh: 每招，長聲呼「某復」，三呼止，投衣於前，承以篋，升自阼階，入以覆尸。

translations.literal: Each beckon, a long call "So-and-so return," three calls and stop, cast the garment forward, received in a box, ascended by the eastern steps, entered to cover the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Each beckon was a long cry of "So-and-so, return!" three times; then the garment was cast down, placed in a box, carried up the east steps, and laid over the corpse.

sentences.zh: 乃設床於室戶內之西，去脚，簟、枕，施幄，去裙。

translations.literal: Then set a couch west within the chamber door, remove footrest, mat and pillow, hang curtains, remove skirt.
translations.idiomatic: A couch was set west inside the chamber door; footrest removed; mat, pillow, and curtains arranged; skirt removed.

sentences.zh: 遷尸於牀，南首，覆用斂衾，去死衣，楔齒以角柶，綴足以燕几，校在南。

translations.literal: Move the corpse to the couch, head south, cover with the shrouding quilt, remove death clothes, wedge teeth with horn spoon, bind feet with swallow bench, staff south.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse was moved south-facing; shrouded; death clothes removed; teeth wedged with a horn spoon; feet bound with a swallow-shaped support; staff placed south.

sentences.zh: 其內外哭位如始死之儀。

translations.literal: Inner and outer places of weeping as at first death.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping positions inside and out matched those at first death.

sentences.zh: 乃奠以脯、醢，酒用吉器。

translations.literal: Then set offering of dried meat and relish, wine in auspicious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings of dried meat and relish were set out, wine in auspicious vessels.

sentences.zh: 升自阼階，奠於尸東當腢。

translations.literal: Ascend by the eastern steps, set offering east of the corpse at the feet.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the east steps and set offerings east of the feet.

sentences.zh: 內喪，則贊者皆受於戶外而設之。

translations.literal: For inner mourning, announcers all received outside the door and set them.
translations.idiomatic: In inner mourning, announcers received items outside the door and set them within.

sentences.zh: 沐浴。

translations.literal: Bathing.
translations.idiomatic: Bathing the corpse.

sentences.zh: 掘埳於階閒，近西，南順，廣尺，長二尺，深三尺，南其壤，為垼竈於西牆下，東向，以俟煮沐。

translations.literal: Dig a pit between the steps, near west, south along, one foot wide, two long, three deep, pile the earth south, make a brick stove under the west wall facing east to await heating the bath.
translations.idiomatic: A pit was dug between the steps near the west, running south, one foot wide, two long, three deep; earth piled south; a brick stove under the west wall faced east to heat bath water.

sentences.zh: 新盆、瓶、六鬲皆濯之，陳於西階下。

translations.literal: New basin, bottle, six tripods all washed, arrayed below the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: New basin, bottle, and six tripods were washed and set below the west steps.

sentences.zh: 沐巾一，浴巾二，用絺若𥿭，實於笲，櫛實於箱若簟，浴衣實於篋，皆具於西序下，南上。

translations.literal: One bathing towel, two drying towels, of fine or coarse cloth, placed in a basket; comb in box or mat; bath robe in chest—all at the west sequence below, ascending south.
translations.idiomatic: One bathing towel and two drying towels of fine or coarse cloth in a basket; comb in a box; bath robe in a chest—all west of the sequence, ranked south to north.

sentences.zh: 水淅稷米，取汁煮之，又汲為湯以俟浴。

translations.literal: Water strained through millet, juice boiled; again draw hot water to await bathing.
translations.idiomatic: Water was strained through millet and boiled; more was drawn as hot water for the bath.

sentences.zh: 以盆盛潘及沐盤，升自西階，授沐者，沐者執潘及盤入。

translations.literal: Basin with rinse water and bathing tray, ascend the west steps, hand to the bather; the bather took basin and tray and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Basin and tray of rinse water were brought up the west steps to the bather, who entered with them.

sentences.zh: 主人皆出於戶東，北面西上；

translations.literal: The host all went out east of the door, facing north ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: The host stood east of the door, facing north, ranked west to east;

sentences.zh: 主婦以下戶西，北面東上。

translations.literal: principal wife and below west of the door, facing north ascending east.
translations.idiomatic: the principal wife and women west of the door, facing north, ranked east to west.

sentences.zh: 俱立哭。

translations.literal: All stood weeping.
translations.idiomatic: All stood and wept.

sentences.zh: 其尊行者，丈夫於主人之東，北面西上；

translations.literal: Senior men, husbands east of the host, facing north ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: Senior men stood east of the host, facing north, west to east;

sentences.zh: 婦人於主婦之西，北面東上。

translations.literal: women west of the principal wife, facing north ascending east.
translations.idiomatic: women west of the principal wife, facing north, east to west.

sentences.zh: 俱坐哭。

translations.literal: All sat weeping.
translations.idiomatic: All sat and wept.

sentences.zh: 婦人以帳。

translations.literal: Women used a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Women screened the body with a canopy.

sentences.zh: 乃沐櫛，束髮用組，挋用巾。

translations.literal: Then comb and bind hair with ties, dry with towel, rub with bath robe.
translations.idiomatic: Hair was combed and bound, dried with a towel, and rubbed with the bath robe.

sentences.zh: 浴則四人抗衾，二人浴，拭用巾，挋用浴衣。

translations.literal: For bathing, four men raised the quilt, two bathed, wiped with towel, rubbed with bath robe.
translations.idiomatic: Four men held the quilt while two bathed the body, wiped it, and dressed it in the bath robe.

sentences.zh: 設牀於尸東，衽下莞上簟。

translations.literal: Set couch east of the corpse, rush mat below, fine mat above.
translations.idiomatic: A couch was set east of the corpse with rush mat below and fine mat above.

sentences.zh: 浴者舉尸，易牀，設枕，翦鬢斷爪如生，盛以小囊，大斂內於棺中。

translations.literal: Bathers lifted the corpse, changed couch, set pillow, trimmed temples and cut nails as in life, placed in a small bag, to be placed in the coffin at great shrouding.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse was lifted to the new couch, pillow set, temples trimmed and nails cut as in life, and clippings placed in a small bag for the great shrouding.

sentences.zh: 楔齒之柶、浴巾，皆埋於埳，寘之。

translations.literal: The tooth-wedge spoon and bathing towels were all buried in the pit and filled in.
translations.idiomatic: The tooth spoon and bathing towels were buried in the pit and filled in.

sentences.zh: 衣以明衣裳，以方巾覆面，仍以大斂之衾覆之。

translations.literal: Clothe in bright inner and outer garments, cover the face with square kerchief, still cover with the great shrouding quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Bright inner and outer garments were put on, the face covered with a square kerchief, then the great shroud.

sentences.zh: 內外入就位，哭。

translations.literal: Inner and outer entered position, wept.
translations.idiomatic: Mourners took their places inside and out and wept.

sentences.zh: 乃襲。

translations.literal: Then investiture dressing.
translations.idiomatic: Then the investiture dressing.

sentences.zh: 襲衣三稱，西領南上，明衣裳，舄一；

translations.literal: Three suits of investiture dress, west collar ascending south, bright garments, one pair of shoes;
translations.idiomatic: Three suits with west collar ranked south to north, bright garments, and one pair of shoes;

sentences.zh: 帛巾一，方尺八寸；

translations.literal: one silk kerchief, one foot eight inches square;
translations.idiomatic: one silk kerchief measuring one foot eight inches square;

sentences.zh: 充耳，白纊；

translations.literal: ear plugs, white silk wadding;
translations.idiomatic: ear plugs of white silk wadding;

sentences.zh: 面衣，玄方尺，纁裏，組繫；

translations.literal: face cloth, black one foot square, red lining, tied with cord;
translations.idiomatic: face cloth, black one foot square with red lining, tied with cord;

sentences.zh: 握手，玄纁裏，長尺二寸，廣五寸，削約於內旁寸，著以綿組繫。

translations.literal: hand object, black and red lining, one foot two long, five inches wide, tapered one inch inside the sides, fastened with silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: hand object of black and red lining, one foot two by five inches, tapered at the sides, bound with silk cord.

sentences.zh: 庶襚繼陳，不用。

translations.literal: Commoners' continued gifts arrayed, not used.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' supplementary gifts were displayed but not used.

sentences.zh: 將襲，具牀席於西階西，內外皆出哭，如浴。

translations.literal: When about to invest, prepare couch and mat west of the west steps; inner and outer all went out weeping, as for bathing.
translations.idiomatic: Before investiture, couch and mat were set west of the west steps; all mourners withdrew and wept as at bathing.

sentences.zh: 襲者以牀升，入設於尸東，布枕席，陳襲於席。

translations.literal: The dresser raised the couch and entered, set east of the corpse, spread pillow and mat, arrayed investiture on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Dressers brought the couch in, set it east of the corpse, spread pillow and mat, and laid out the investiture garments.

sentences.zh: 祝去巾，加面衣，設充耳、握手，納舄若履。

translations.literal: The invoker removed the kerchief, added face cloth, set ear plugs and hand object, put on shoes or sandals.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker removed the kerchief, added face cloth, ear plugs, and hand object, and put on shoes.

sentences.zh: 既襲，覆以大斂之衾，內外入哭。

translations.literal: After investiture, cover with the great shrouding quilt; inner and outer entered weeping.
translations.idiomatic: After investiture, the great shroud was laid on; mourners re-entered and wept.

sentences.zh: 乃唅。

translations.literal: Then placing pearls in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the mouth-pearl rite.

sentences.zh: 贊者奉盤水及笲，一品至于三品，飯用粱，唅用璧；

translations.literal: Announcer bore tray of water and basket; first to third rank, rice grain for filling, pearls for mouth;
translations.idiomatic: An announcer brought water and a basket. Ranks one to three used millet for filling and jade disks for the mouth;

sentences.zh: 四品至于五品，飯用稷；

translations.literal: fourth to fifth rank, millet for filling;
translations.idiomatic: ranks four to five used millet;

sentences.zh: 唅用碧；

translations.literal: mouth with green jade;
translations.idiomatic: green jade for the mouth;

sentences.zh: 六品至于九品，飯用粱，唅用貝。

translations.literal: sixth to ninth rank, millet for filling, shell for mouth.
translations.idiomatic: ranks six to nine used millet and shells.

sentences.zh: 升堂，唅者盥手於戶外，洗粱、璧實於笲，執以入，祝從入，北面，徹枕，去衾，受笲，奠於尸東。

translations.literal: Ascend the hall; the filler washed hands outside the door, washed millet and disks in the basket, carried in; invoker followed in, faced north, removed pillow, removed quilt, received basket, set east of the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the hall, the filler washed outside, prepared millet and disks in the basket, and entered with the invoker, who faced north, removed pillow and quilt, received the basket, and set it east of the corpse.

sentences.zh: 唅者坐於牀東，西面，鑿巾，納飯、唅於尸口。

translations.literal: The filler sat east of the couch facing west, opened the kerchief, placed rice and pearls in the corpse's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The filler sat east of the couch facing west, opened the kerchief, and placed grain and pearls in the mouth.

sentences.zh: 既唅，主人復位。

translations.literal: After placing pearls, the host returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: After the mouth rite, the host returned to station.

sentences.zh: 乃為明旌，以絳廣充幅，一品至于三品，長九尺，韜杠，銘曰「某官封之柩」，置於西階上；

translations.literal: Then make the bright banner, crimson cloth full width; first to third rank, nine feet long, wrapped on the pole, inscription "Such-and-such office's coffin," placed on the west steps;
translations.idiomatic: A bright banner of crimson cloth was made: ranks one to three, nine feet, wrapped on the pole, inscribed "Coffin of such-and-such office," and set on the west steps;

sentences.zh: 四品至于五品，長八尺；

translations.literal: fourth to fifth rank, eight feet;
translations.idiomatic: ranks four to five, eight feet;

sentences.zh: 六品至于九品，長六尺。

translations.literal: sixth to ninth rank, six feet.
translations.idiomatic: ranks six to nine, six feet.

sentences.zh: 鑿木為重，一品至于三品，長八尺，橫者半之，三分庭一在南；

translations.literal: Carve wood for the spirit frame; first to third rank, eight feet long, crosspiece half that, one-third of the courtyard south;
translations.idiomatic: A wooden spirit frame was carved: ranks one to three, eight feet with crosspiece half as long, set one-third into the south courtyard;

sentences.zh: 四品至于五品，長七尺；

translations.literal: fourth to fifth rank, seven feet;
translations.idiomatic: ranks four to five, seven feet;

sentences.zh: 六品至于九品，長六尺。

translations.literal: sixth to ninth rank, six feet.
translations.idiomatic: ranks six to nine, six feet.

sentences.zh: 以沐之米為粥，實於鬲，蓋以疏布，繫以竹蔤，縣於重木。

translations.literal: Use the bathing millet as gruel, fill the tripod, cover with open-weave cloth, tie with bamboo sheath, hang on the spirit frame wood.
translations.idiomatic: Bathing millet was made into gruel in a tripod, covered with open cloth, tied with bamboo, and hung on the frame.

sentences.zh: 覆用葦席，北面，屈兩端交後，西端在上，綴以竹蔤。

translations.literal: Cover with rush mat, north face, bend both ends crossed behind, west end above, tie with bamboo sheath.
translations.idiomatic: A rush mat covered it, north-facing, ends crossed behind with the west end above, tied with bamboo.

sentences.zh: 祝取銘置於重，殯堂前楹下，夾以葦席。

translations.literal: The invoker took the inscription and placed it on the frame before the hall pillars, flanked with rush mats.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker set the inscription on the frame under the hall pillars, flanked by rush mats.

sentences.zh: 小斂衣一十九稱，朝服一，笏一，陳於東序，西領北上。

translations.literal: Small shrouding nineteen suits of clothes, one court dress, one tablet, arrayed in the east sequence, west collar ascending north.
translations.idiomatic: Small shrouding: nineteen suits, one court dress, one tablet, arrayed in the east sequence, west collar ranked north to south.

sentences.zh: 設奠於東堂下，甒二，實以醴、酒，觶二，角柶一，少牢、腊三，籩、豆俎各八。

translations.literal: Set offering below the east hall, two earthen jars with ale and wine, two goblets, one horn spoon, three sets of young livestock and cured meat, eight baskets and dishes and trays each.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings below the east hall: two jars of ale and wine, two goblets, one horn spoon, three trays of livestock and cured meat, eight baskets, dishes, and trays each.

sentences.zh: 設盆盥於饌東，布巾。

translations.literal: Set basin and washstand east of the food, cloth towel.
translations.idiomatic: Basin and washstand east of the food, with a cloth towel.

sentences.zh: 贊者辟脯醢之，奠於尸牀西南。

translations.literal: Announcer arranged dried meat and relish, set offering southwest of the corpse couch.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer arranged dried meat and relish southwest of the corpse couch.

sentences.zh: 乃斂。

translations.literal: Then shroud.
translations.idiomatic: Then shrouding.

sentences.zh: 具牀席於堂西，設盆盥西階之西，如東方。

translations.literal: Prepare couch and mat west of the hall, set basin west of the west steps, as on the east side.
translations.idiomatic: Couch and mat were prepared west of the hall; basin and washstand west of the west steps, mirroring the east.

sentences.zh: 斂者盥，與執服者以斂衣入，喪者東西皆少退，內外哭。

translations.literal: Shrouders washed, entered with shrouding clothes with dressers, mourners east and west all stepped back slightly, inner and outer wept.
translations.idiomatic: Shrouders washed, entered with garments; mourners east and west stepped back; all wept.

sentences.zh: 已斂，覆以夷衾，設牀於堂上兩楹間，衽下莞上簟，有枕。

translations.literal: After shrouding, cover with the plain quilt, set couch between the two hall pillars, rush below fine mat above, with pillow.
translations.idiomatic: After shrouding, a plain quilt covered the body; a couch between the hall pillars had rush below, fine mat and pillow above.

sentences.zh: 卒斂，開帷，主人以下西面憑哭，主婦以下東面憑哭，退。

translations.literal: When shrouding ended, open curtains; host and below faced west leaning and wept, principal wife and below east leaning and wept, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When shrouding ended, curtains opened; the host and men leaned westward and wept, the wife and women eastward, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乃斂髮而奠。

translations.literal: Then bind hair and set offering.
translations.idiomatic: Then hair was bound and offerings set.

sentences.zh: 贊者盥手奉饌至階，升，設於尸東，醴、酒奠於饌南，西上，其俎，祝受巾巾之。

translations.literal: Announcer washed hands, bore food to the steps, ascended, set east of the corpse, ale and wine south of the food ascending west, for the trays the invoker received towel and covered them.
translations.idiomatic: An announcer washed, brought food up the steps, set it east of the corpse with ale and wine south of it; the invoker covered the trays with a towel.

sentences.zh: 奠者徹襲，奠，自西階降出。

translations.literal: The setter removed investiture, set offering, descended the west steps and went out.
translations.idiomatic: The setter removed investiture garments, set the offering, and left by the west steps.

sentences.zh: 下帷，內外俱坐哭。

translations.literal: Lower curtains; inner and outer all sat weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains were lowered; all sat and wept.

sentences.zh: 有國官、僚佐者，以官代哭；

translations.literal: Where there were state officials and aides, officials wept in rotation;
translations.idiomatic: If state officials and aides were present, they took turns weeping at post;

sentences.zh: 無者，以親疏為之。

translations.literal: where none, kin by closeness did so.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise kin by degree of relationship took turns.

sentences.zh: 夜則為燎於庭，厥明滅燎。

translations.literal: At night set torches in the courtyard; at dawn extinguish torches.
translations.idiomatic: Torches were lit in the courtyard at night and extinguished at dawn.

sentences.zh: 乃大斂。

translations.literal: Then great shrouding.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the great shrouding.

sentences.zh: 衣三十稱，上服一稱，冕具簪、導、纓，內喪則有花釵，衾一，西領南上。

translations.literal: Thirty suits of clothes, one upper suit, crown with pin, guide, and tassel; for inner mourning there were flower hairpins; one quilt, west collar ascending south.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty suits, one upper suit with crown, pin, guide, and tassel; inner mourning added flower hairpins; one quilt, west collar ranked south to north.

sentences.zh: 設奠如小斂，甒加勺，篚在東南，籩、豆、俎皆有冪，用功布。

translations.literal: Set offering as small shrouding; jars with ladles, baskets southeast, baskets, dishes, and trays all with covers, using work cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings matched small shrouding; jars with ladles; baskets southeast; all baskets, dishes, and trays covered in work cloth.

sentences.zh: 棺入，內外皆止哭，升棺於殯所，乃哭。

translations.literal: Coffin entered; inner and outer all stopped weeping; raised coffin to the encoffining place, then wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin arrived, weeping ceased; it was raised to the encoffining hall, then weeping resumed.

sentences.zh: 熬八篚，黍、稷、粱、稻各二，皆加魚、腊。

translations.literal: Eight baskets of grain, two each of millet, panic millet, fine millet, and rice, all with fish and cured meat added.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grain baskets—two each of millet, panic millet, fine millet, and rice—with fish and cured meat added.

sentences.zh: 燭俟於饌東，設盆盥於東階東南。

translations.literal: Candles awaited east of the food; basin and washstand southeast of the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: Candles stood east of the food; basin and washstand southeast of the east steps.

sentences.zh: 祝盥訖，升自阼階，徹巾，執巾者以待於阼階下。

translations.literal: After the invoker washed, ascended the east steps, removed the kerchief; the kerchief holder awaited below the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker washed, ascended the east steps, and removed the kerchief; the holder waited below.

sentences.zh: 祝盥、贊者徹小斂之饌，降自西階，設於序西南，當西霤，如設於堂上。

translations.literal: Invoker washed; announcer removed small-shrouding food, descended west steps, set southwest of the sequence at the west eaves, as when set in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker washed; announcers removed small-shrouding food down the west steps to the southwest of the west eaves, as in the hall.

sentences.zh: 乃適於東階下新饌所，帷堂內外皆少退，立哭。

translations.literal: Then went to the new food place below the east steps; curtains in hall inside and outside all stepped back slightly, stood weeping.
translations.idiomatic: They moved to the new food below the east steps; curtains drawn, mourners stepped back and stood weeping.

sentences.zh: 御者斂，加冠若花釵，覆以衾。

translations.literal: Attendants shrouded, added crown or flower hairpin, covered with quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants shrouded the body, added crown or hairpins, and covered it with the quilt.

sentences.zh: 開帷，喪者東西憑哭如小斂，諸親憑哭。

translations.literal: Open curtains; mourners east and west leaned weeping as at small shrouding; kin leaned weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains opened; mourners leaned and wept east and west as at small shrouding.

sentences.zh: 斂者四人舉牀，男女從，奉尸斂於棺，乃加蓋，覆以夷衾，內外皆復位如初。

translations.literal: Four shrouders raised the couch; men and women followed, bore the corpse into the coffin, then added the lid, covered with plain quilt, inner and outer all returned to position as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Four bearers lifted the couch; kin followed and placed the corpse in the coffin, added the lid, covered it, and mourners returned to station.

sentences.zh: 設熬穀，首足各一篚，傍各三篚，以木覆棺上，乃塗之，設帟於殯上，祝取銘置于殯。

translations.literal: Set grain baskets, one at head and foot, three each at the sides, wood over the coffin, then plastered, set canopy on the bier, invoker took inscription and placed on the bier.
translations.idiomatic: Grain baskets were set at head and foot and three on each side; wood was laid over the coffin and plastered; a canopy covered the bier; the invoker set the inscription upon it.

sentences.zh: 乃奠。

translations.literal: Then offering.
translations.idiomatic: Then offerings.

sentences.zh: 執巾、几席者升自阼階，入設於室之西南隅，東面。

translations.literal: Kerchief and couch bearers ascended the east steps, entered and set southwest corner of the chamber, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers of kerchief, couch, and mat entered by the east steps and set them in the southwest corner facing east.

sentences.zh: 又几、巾已加，贊者以饌升，入室，西面，設於席前。

translations.literal: When couch and kerchief were added, announcer bore food up, entered the chamber facing west, set before the mat.
translations.idiomatic: When couch and kerchief were in place, announcers brought food in facing west before the mat.

sentences.zh: 祝加巾於俎，奠者降自西階以出。

translations.literal: Invoker added kerchief to the tray; setter descended west steps and went out.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker covered the tray with a kerchief; the setter left by the west steps.

sentences.zh: 下帷，內外皆就位哭。

translations.literal: Lower curtains; inner and outer all took position weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains lowered; mourners took their stations and wept.

sentences.zh: 既殯，設靈座於下室西閒，東向，施牀、几、桉、屏、帳、服飾，以時上膳羞及湯沐如平生。

translations.literal: After encoffining, set spirit seat in the west chamber of the lower hall, facing east; set couch, table, desk, screen, canopy, dress and ornaments; at the proper times offer food and hot water as in life.
translations.idiomatic: After encoffining, a spirit seat faced east in the west chamber of the lower hall, furnished as in life; meals and hot water were offered on schedule.

sentences.zh: 殷奠之日，不饋於下室。

translations.literal: On days of generous offering, no food in the lower chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On generous-offering days, no food was served in the lower chamber.

sentences.zh: 廬在殯堂東廊下，近南，設苫凷。

translations.literal: Mourning hut east of the encoffining hall corridor near south, set rush and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning hut stood in the east corridor of the encoffining hall near the south, floored with rush and earth.

sentences.zh: 齊衰於其南，為堊室，俱北戶，翦蒲為席，不緣；

translations.literal: Equal hemp south of it, whitewashed chamber, both north-facing doors, rush mats cut square, unedged;
translations.idiomatic: Equal hemp mourners south of that in a whitewashed chamber, both doors north-facing, square-cut rush mats without edging;

sentences.zh: 大功又於其南，張帷，席以蒲；

translations.literal: greater hemp further south, hung curtains, rush mats;
translations.idiomatic: greater hemp further south under hung curtains on rush mats;

sentences.zh: 小功、緦麻又於其南，設牀，席以蒲。

translations.literal: lesser hemp and finest hemp further south, set couch, rush mat.
translations.idiomatic: lesser and finest hemp further south on couches with rush mats.

sentences.zh: 婦人次於西房。

translations.literal: Women next in the west chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Women mourned next in the west chamber.

sentences.zh: 三日成服，內外皆哭，盡哀。

translations.literal: On the third day complete dress; inner and outer all wept, exhausting grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day mourning dress was completed; all wept to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 乃降就次，服其服，無服者仍素服。

translations.literal: Then descended to the hut, wore their dress; those without dress still wore plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They then moved to the huts in proper dress; those without mourning dress remained in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 相者引主人以下俱杖升，立於殯，內外皆哭。

translations.literal: The director led host and below, all with staffs, to ascend and stand at the bier; inner and outer wept.
translations.idiomatic: A director led the host and others, staffs in hand, to the bier; all wept.

sentences.zh: 諸子孫跪哭尊者之前，祖父撫之，女子子對立而哭，唯諸父不撫。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons knelt weeping before elders; grandfather stroked them; daughters faced each other weeping—only paternal uncles did not stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons knelt before elders to weep; grandfathers stroked them; daughters faced one another—paternal uncles did not stroke.

sentences.zh: 尊者出，主人以下降立阼階。

translations.literal: When elders went out, host and below descended to stand at the east steps.
translations.idiomatic: When elders left, the host and others descended to the east steps.

sentences.zh: 朔望殷奠，饌於東堂下，瓦甒二，實醴及酒，角觶二，木柶一，少牢及腊三俎，二簋、二簠、二鈃，六籩、六豆。

translations.literal: On new and full moon generous offerings, food below the east hall, two pottery jars with ale and wine, two horn goblets, one wooden spoon, three trays of young livestock and cured meat, two grain baskets, two square baskets, two bells, six baskets and six dishes.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moons, offerings below the east hall included two jars of ale and wine, horn goblets, a wooden spoon, livestock and cured meat, grain baskets, bells, baskets, and dishes.

sentences.zh: 其日，不饋於下室。

translations.literal: On that day, no food in the lower chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On those days, no food was served in the lower chamber.

sentences.zh: 葬有期，前一日之夕，除葦障，設賓次於大門外之右，南向。

translations.literal: When burial had a set date, the evening before remove rush screens, set guest tents outside the great gate to the right, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of burial, rush screens were removed and guest tents pitched south-facing outside the great gate to the right.

sentences.zh: 啟殯之日，主人及諸子皆去冠，以衺巾帕頭，就位哭。

translations.literal: On the day of opening the bier, host and sons all removed caps, wore slanted kerchief headwrap, took position weeping.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the bier was opened, host and sons removed caps for slanted kerchiefs and took up weeping stations.

sentences.zh: 祝衰服執功布，升自東階，詣殯南，北向，內外止哭，三聲噫嘻，乃曰：「謹以吉辰啟殯。

translations.literal: Invoker in mourning dress held work cloth, ascended east steps to south of the bier facing north; inner and outer stopped weeping, three sounds of sigh, then said: "Respectfully on this auspicious day open the bier.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker in mourning dress ascended the east steps north of the bier and announced: "On this auspicious day we respectfully open the bier."

sentences.zh: 」既告，內外哭。

translations.literal: " After announcing, inner and outer wept.
translations.idiomatic: After the announcement, all wept.

sentences.zh: 祝取銘置於重。

translations.literal: Invoker took inscription and placed on the frame.
translations.idiomatic: The invoker set the inscription on the spirit frame.

sentences.zh: 掌事者升，徹殯塗，設席於柩東，升柩於席。

translations.literal: Stewards ascended, removed encoffining plaster, set mat east of the coffin, raised coffin to the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards removed the plaster, set a mat east of the coffin, and raised the coffin onto it.

sentences.zh: 又設席柩東，祝以功布升，拂柩，覆用夷衾，周設帷，開戶東向。

translations.literal: Again set mat east of coffin; invoker with work cloth ascended, dusted coffin, covered with plain quilt, curtains all around, opened door facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Another mat was set east of the coffin; the invoker dusted it, covered it, hung curtains, and opened the door eastward.

sentences.zh: 主人以下升，哭於帷東，西向，俱南上。

translations.literal: Host and below ascended, wept east of the curtains facing west, all ascending south.
translations.idiomatic: The host and others ascended and wept west of the curtains, ranked south to north.

sentences.zh: 諸祖父以下哭於帷東北壁下，諸祖母以下哭於帷西北壁下；

translations.literal: Grandfathers and below wept northeast of the curtains; grandmothers and below northwest;
translations.idiomatic: Grandfathers wept northeast of the curtains; grandmothers northwest;

sentences.zh: 外姻丈夫帷東上，婦人帷西。

translations.literal: outer-affinal men east above the curtains; women west.
translations.idiomatic: male affines east above the curtains; women west.

sentences.zh: 祝與進饌者各以奠升，設於柩東席上，祝酌醴奠之。

translations.literal: Invoker and food bearers each ascended with offerings, set on the mat east of the coffin; invoker poured ale and set offering.
translations.idiomatic: Invokers and food bearers set offerings on the mat east of the coffin; the invoker poured ale.

sentences.zh: 陳器用。

translations.literal: Array implements for use.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary implements were arrayed.

sentences.zh: 啟之夕，發引前五刻，搥一鼓為一嚴，陳布吉、凶儀仗，方相、誌石、大棺車及明器以下，陳於柩車之前。

translations.literal: On the evening of opening, five watches before the procession, one drum-strike for first vigil, array auspicious and inauspicious guards, exorcist, epitaph stone, great coffin cart and spirit objects below, all before the coffin cart.
translations.idiomatic: On opening night, five watches before departure, the first vigil drum sounded; auspicious and inauspicious guards, exorcist, epitaph, great coffin cart, and spirit goods were arrayed before the coffin cart.

sentences.zh: 一品引四、披六、鐸左右各八、黼翣二、黻翣二、畫翣二，二品三品引二、披四、鐸左右各六、黼翣二、畫翣二，四品五品引二、披二、鐸左右各四、黼翣二、畫翣二，六品至于九品披二、鐸二、畫翣二。

translations.literal: First rank: four pullers, six pallbearers, eight bells each side, two brocade feather fans, two embroidered feather fans, two painted feather fans; second and third rank: two pullers, four pallbearers, six bells each side, two brocade fans, two painted fans; fourth and fifth: two pullers, two pallbearers, four bells each side, two brocade fans, two painted fans; sixth to ninth: two pallbearers, two bells, two painted fans.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: four pullers, six pallbearers, eight bells per side, brocade, embroidered, and painted feather fans; second and third ranks reduced accordingly; fourth and fifth further reduced; sixth through ninth: two pallbearers, two bells, two painted fans.

sentences.zh: 二刻頃，搥二鼓為二嚴，掌饌者徹啟奠以出，內外俱立哭。

translations.literal: After about two quarters, second drum for second vigil; food stewards removed opening offerings and went out; inner and outer all stood weeping.
translations.idiomatic: After about two quarters, the second vigil drum sounded; stewards removed opening offerings; all stood weeping.

sentences.zh: 執紼者皆入，掌事者徹帷，持翣者升，以翣障柩。

translations.literal: Cord holders all entered; stewards removed curtains; fan holders ascended and screened the coffin with fans.
translations.idiomatic: Cord holders entered; stewards removed curtains; fan bearers screened the coffin.

sentences.zh: 執紼者升，執鐸者夾西階立，執纛者入，當西階南，北面立。

translations.literal: Cord holders ascended; bell holders stood flanking the west steps; banner holders entered, stood south of the west steps facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Cord holders ascended; bell men flanked the west steps; banner men stood south of them facing north.

sentences.zh: 掌事者取重出，倚於門外之東。

translations.literal: Stewards took the frame out and leaned it east outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards carried the spirit frame out and set it east of the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 執旌者立於纛南，北面。

translations.literal: Banner holders stood south of the great banner facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Banner bearers stood south of the great banner, facing north.

sentences.zh: 搥三鼓為三嚴，靈車進於內門外，南向，祝以腰輿詣靈座前，西向跪告。

translations.literal: Third drum for third vigil; spirit cart advanced to inside the inner gate facing south; invoker with litter went before the spirit seat facing west kneeling to announce.
translations.idiomatic: At the third vigil drum, the spirit cart waited inside the inner gate facing south; the invoker knelt west before the spirit seat to announce.

sentences.zh: 腰輿降自西階，以詣靈車。

translations.literal: Litter descended the west steps to the spirit cart.
translations.idiomatic: The litter came down the west steps to the spirit cart.

sentences.zh: 腰輿退。

translations.literal: Litter withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The litter withdrew.

sentences.zh: 執鐸者振鐸，降就階間，南向。

translations.literal: Bell holders sounded bells, descended to between the steps facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Bell men sounded the bells and descended between the steps facing south.

sentences.zh: 持翣者障以翣。

translations.literal: Fan holders screened with fans.
translations.idiomatic: Fan bearers screened the coffin with fans.

sentences.zh: 執纛者却行而引，輴止則北面立；

translations.literal: Banner holders walked backward leading; when the bier stopped they faced north standing;
translations.idiomatic: Banner men walked backward leading; when the bier halted they faced north;

sentences.zh: 執旌者亦漸而南，輴止，北面。

translations.literal: banner holders also gradually south; when bier stopped, faced north.
translations.idiomatic: banner bearers moved south gradually; when the bier halted, they faced north.

sentences.zh: 主人以下以次從。

translations.literal: Host and below followed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The host and others followed in order.

sentences.zh: 輴在庭。

translations.literal: Bier in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The bier rested in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 輴至庭，主人及諸子以下立哭於輴東北，西向南上；

translations.literal: When the bier reached the courtyard, host and sons and below stood weeping northeast of the bier, facing west ascending south;
translations.idiomatic: In the courtyard the host and sons wept northeast of the bier, facing west, ranked south to north;

sentences.zh: 祖父以下立哭於輴東北，南向西上；

translations.literal: grandfather and below northeast of the bier, facing south ascending west;
translations.idiomatic: grandfathers northeast, facing south, ranked west to east;

sentences.zh: 異姓之丈夫立哭於主人東南，西面北上。

translations.literal: unrelated men southeast of the host, facing west ascending north.
translations.idiomatic: unrelated men southeast of the host, facing west, ranked north to south.

sentences.zh: 婦人以次從降，妻、妾、女子子以下立哭於輴西，東面南上；

translations.literal: Women followed in order down; wife, concubines, daughters and below west of the bier, facing east ascending south;
translations.idiomatic: Women followed: wife, concubines, and daughters west of the bier facing east, south to north;

sentences.zh: 祖母以下立哭於輴西北，南向東上；

translations.literal: grandmother and below northwest of the bier, facing south ascending east;
translations.idiomatic: grandmothers northwest, facing south, east to west;

sentences.zh: 異姓之婦人立哭於主婦西南，東面北上。

translations.literal: unrelated women southwest of the principal wife, facing east ascending north.
translations.idiomatic: unrelated women southwest of the principal wife, facing east, north to south.

sentences.zh: 內外之際，障以行帷。

translations.literal: Between inner and outer, screened by traveling curtain.
